newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua vote dispute sparks death threats.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua vote dispute sparks death threats.

text.p: A human rights group on Friday said prominent Nicaraguan political and religious figures had received death threats by telephone following the disputed Oct. 20 elections.

Among those threatened were President Violeta Chamorro, the head of the Catholic Church in Nicaragua Cardinal Miguel Obando y Bravo, Supreme Election Council president Rosa Marina Zelaya and the nation's Comptroller Agustin Jarquin.
"We categorically reject these actions that create fear and instability and further polarise Nicaraguan society," the president of the Nicaraguan Human Rights Centre, Vilma Nunez, told Reuters.
As head of the highest electoral authority, Zelaya has been at the centre of a political storm since the left-wing Sandinista Front charged the election was fraudulent.
Police have increased security around Zelaya, who will announce a ruling on a Sandinista appeal on Nov. 20.
The final vote count gave Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance an easy 51 percent to 37.7 percent lead over Sandinista leader and former President Daniel Ortega.

Nicaragua's conservative and powerful cardinal, Obando y Bravo, is locked in a war of words with Ortega, who accused the cardinal of interfering in the election process in favour of Aleman in his pre-vote speeches from the pulpit.

So far none of the threats have led to attacks, but Nicaragua's Comptroller's Office, which is carrying out a number of high-profile corruption investigations, had to be evacuated on Tuesday after receiving a bomb threat.
Nunez said she did not know if the threats were the work of individuals or a systematic campaign, but urged election authorities to hurry up and confirm the election's winners.
She said delay in ending the election process created a climate of tension and uncertainty conducive to such threats.
